test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about the loudness and softness of a sound wave?

(i) A loud sound has less amplitude as compared to a soft sound.
(ii) A loud sound has more energy associated with it as compared to a soft sound.
(iii) The loudness of a sound wave is the measure of the response of the ear to the sound.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (ii) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Loudness and Amplitude**: The loudness of a sound is determined by the **amplitude** of the sound wave. A sound wave with a **larger amplitude** results in a **louder sound**, whereas a wave with a **smaller amplitude** produces a **soft or feeble sound**. Because a loud sound requires a greater displacement of particles, it possesses a higher amplitude than a soft sound. ***Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.***
 
• **Energy in Sound Waves**: Sound is a form of **mechanical energy** that propagates through a medium. The **energy** carried by a sound wave is directly proportional to the **square of its amplitude**. Since loud sounds have larger amplitudes, they carry significantly **more energy** compared to soft sounds. ***Hence, statement (ii) is correct.***
